uncertainty: Twelve pinned open-source PDF reader package paths passed the valid one-page local PDF control: Poppler C++, PoDoFo, qpdf, MuPDF, Ghostscript, PDFio, PDFium, PDF-Writer, PDF4QT, Qt PDF, Xpdf, and pdfmm. Pdfmm 0.10.0 is a distinct source release and C++ API forked from PoDoFo, and shares that parser lineage. Xpdf 4.06 provides a source CMake object-library target with PDFDoc(char* local file) and getNumPages(); the verifier archives that target and links its source-built goo and fofi libraries. Xpdf does not publish a separately installed libxpdf artifact or promise a stable ABI, and this path is explicitly a source library use. Qt PDF exposes a native QPdfDocument C++17 local file loader in the separate QtWebEngine package and shares PDFium underneath; it is counted as one distinct package path. The separate poppler-qt6 formula was excluded as a second frontend of the same Poppler source package already counted. PDF4QT is a native C++20 API built from pinned source and Blend2D with a recorded macOS core-only compatibility patch. MuPDF, Ghostscript, PDFio, and PDFium are C APIs called directly from C++17. PDFium additionally loaded the first page; its immutable distributor release artifact is SHA-256 pinned, its original public API header matches canonical PDFium source revision 6688c576fd851f4159c6fae39396da50939de110, and its prebuilt binary is SHA-256 checked. The distributor release claims chromium/8152; the header match alone does not prove every binary source file equals the observed upstream revision. QtWebEngine 6.11.2_1 installs a QtPdf framework whose official v6.11.2 header matches byte for byte and whose binary is pinned; its Qt6Pdf.pc reports 6.12.0 and that discrepancy is recorded. Eight more verified package paths are needed for the 20-path working goal. Four Homebrew formula-name searches captured exact fuzzy windows of 38, 4, 4, and 2 hits; they are discovery leads, not proof or usage rankings. The Conan Center Index tree API was rate limited, so its complete recipe-name surface is not claimed; targeted Conan pages were checked. PDFio, PDF-Writer, PDF4QT, and Qt PDF came from official documentation outside Homebrew hits. One plausible lead, cpdflib, remains unresolved: its tagged v2.5.2a binary is noncommercial and ineligible; a tagged AGPL C/C++ library release has not been established. qpdf, PDF4QT, PDF-Writer, PoDoFo, PDFio, and pdfmm have exact primary GitHub star counts; Poppler, MuPDF, Ghostscript, PDFium, Qt PDF, and Xpdf have canonical non-GitHub upstreams and remain unranked. Five installed libraries and headers are checked against pinned source archives, PDFio, PDF-Writer, PDF4QT, Xpdf, and pdfmm are source-built, Qt PDF is a hash-pinned installed framework, and PDFium uses a pinned distributor binary. qpdf uses upstream 12.4.2 and Homebrew bottle revision 12.4.2_1. The ISO C++ standard library has no documented PDF parser. The control covers a simple unencrypted one-page PDF only. No malformed-input, vulnerability, or resource-use experiments were run.
